title: Dandelion and Mimi's Sweet Dream
markdown:
Once, on a sleepy moonlit evening, a little duckling named Dandelion lived by a lily pond. He was wonderfully soft and fluffy. He loved a gentle paddle among the pads. Always nearby, with happy little bounces, was Mimi the kitten. Her fur was as soft as dandelion seeds. Her whiskers wiggled when she smelled something interesting.

Tonight a sweet warm smell floated on the air. It was like cookies kissed by the sun, mixed with vanilla.

“Oh, Mimi,” quacked Dandelion, soft as a ripple. “Do you smell that? It smells like vanilla clouds coming in for a cuddle.”

Mimi’s whiskers danced. “Mrow. Yes. Yummy and warm. And a little bit far.” Her purr started, a small rumble. “It smells like a happy dream that forgot to come home.”

Dandelion looked around. The world felt soft and quiet. He wriggled his tail and found a hole in his own sleepy thoughts. His favourite giggly dream — the one where he bounced on the biggest greenest lily pads — was not there.

“My happy dream,” he peeped. “It must have floated away.”

He almost rushed into the dark meadow, quacking loud enough to wake the reeds. Mimi nuzzled his fuzzy back.

“Don’t worry your soft feathers. We will find it together. The vanilla smell will lead us. Softly.”

So, wing-in-paw, they followed the scent. Not far. Just to the edge of the whispering meadow, where fireflies winked like tiny fallen stars. The smell grew stronger, like a warm hug. There, in the softest green clover, Dandelion’s happy dream rested, a gentle light.

“There it is,” he quacked, warm with relief.

Mimi blinked. “It looks peaceful. It will be cozier in your sleepy head.”

Dandelion wanted to scoop it up fast, before the breeze took it again. He remembered Mimi’s softly. Very carefully, as if the dream were a bubble, he nudged it with his beak. Mimi gave a feathery push with her paw. The dream shimmered, then floated up, following the faint vanilla trail back toward Dandelion’s mind.

A warm happy feeling spread from his beak to his toes, like a yawn that reached his tail.

The vanilla faded. The meadow grew quieter still. Dandelion’s eyes grew heavy. Mimi curled into a warm ball beside him, her purr a lullaby. Moonbeams laid silver stripes on the grass.

They had followed the smell. They had found the little dream. They had brought it home without a hurry.

And so a lost happy thing comes home when you go after it softly, and share the way.
